The outstanding Chinese- and Thai-inspired menu has many choices, including gluten-free options. The flavors confirm the freshness and care typical of Big Bowl. This particular location has exceptional service. What a gem!

For those unfamiliar with the menu, the starters are hard to beat. If you are unsure, share the chopped salad (I'm pretty sure that they will substitute tofu for those who do not want to grilled checked). The egg rolls are fresh, house-made, and ample.

For main courses, the Chinese items are available with noodles, white rice, or brown rice. The Sesame Chicken is a winner, but if you want to have a treat, the Shrimp and Scallops are fantastic. Big Bowl's scallops are fresh and served to perfection. The consistency with the latter speaks volumes about this place, and I would hope that others have the same experience.  For those who like vegetarian choices, try  the Pad Thai, one of the signature dishes at this restaurant. It's a wonderfully constructed dish that will delight even carnivores because of the flavors and textures.  Other items include the stir-fry rice dishes, that have their own attraction. I like the garlic tofu with fried rice, but the dish is also available with chicken. Either way, it's hard to go wrong.

Let me tell you a story. Back in 2002 when I was just a promising young teen I would dream of soaring into the stars. I would gaze upon the endless vacuum that is space and wonder if we are truly alone; if we are really God's creation or just a small blue speck in a ocean of space. I needed answers to all of life's questions and I knew only one place could give me the satisfaction that I yearned for. That place is No Thai here in beautiful East Lansing. Within the bustling campus of Michigan State University lives a small island of Thai inspired goodness. Never have I witnessed such grace and care for a restaurant than when I walk through those hallowed doors. A small blanket of happiness and peace engulfs me as arrive and my mood instantly gets better from whatever stress my daily life has bestowed upon me. The food is cooked with the care only compared to a Buddhist monk caring for his temple. The concentration for perfection rivals that of Randy Johnson on the pitchers mound on May 18th, 2004 against the Atlanta Braves. Nothing compares to No Thai. It is my religion, my sanctuary, my release. I am forever grateful for this haven of deliciousness and delight. Thank you.

Was looking for a great Thai restaurant near me in Hamburg, typically we will trek out to Plymouth MI for Thai Ocha, but I am so glad we found this place bc it's a bit closer. My hubs ordered the Fried Rice with beef and shrimp and I ordered the Drunken Noodles with tofu. They didn't ask my husband what "flame" he wanted they automatically marked him down for mild. So when I ordered I said "drunken noodles, tofu, medium flame". I'm pretty sure the guy is used to white ladies like myself ordering like I'm some kind of spice expert bc he immediately followed up my order with "are you sure - have you had OUR medium before"? I studied his face for a moment before taking my brave risk "yes, we gotta try it". He smiled and away he went with our order. As an appetizer I ordered the Tom Kha soup (a coconut veggie soup with huge chunks of mushrooms, tomato, chives) and some fried dumplings. Both were superb. Then our main dishes came out. Both plates had enough food to feed an extra couple at the table. The flavor is sooooo authentic and savory yummy. I dug four huge forkfuls of Drunken Noodle into my mouth before it hit me. This place cooks with authentic chilis, not the kind you get at a fast food Thai place that claims it is hot and on the first bite your tongue burns and then fizzles. No. This place has what you need. My mouth was sizzling and my husband turned red and was sweating from the heat of these drunken noodles. He was grateful the chef rightfully guessed he would like his meal "mild flame". The only reason I didn't finish my plate was because it was soooooo hot. But I LOVED it. We will definitely be back there! Likely tomorrow for more 🥰 Thai Cafe - can't wait to see you again soon!!!

My hubs ordered the Fried Rice with beef and shrimp and I ordered the Drunken Noodles with tofu. They didn't ask my husband what "flame" he wanted they automatically marked him down for mild. So when I ordered I said "drunken noodles, tofu, medium flame". I'm pretty sure the guy is used to white ladies like myself ordering like I'm some kind of spice expert bc he immediately followed up my order with "are you sure - have you had OUR medium before"? I studied his face for a moment before taking my brave risk "yes, we gotta try it". He smiled and away he went with our order. As an appetizer I ordered the Tom Kha soup (a coconut veggie soup with huge chunks of mushrooms, tomato, chives) and some fried dumplings. Both were superb. Then our main dishes came out. Both plates had enough food to feed an extra couple at the table. The flavor is sooooo authentic and savory yummy. I dug four huge forkfuls of Drunken Noodle into my mouth before it hit me. This place cooks with authentic chilis, not the kind you get at a fast food Thai place that claims it is hot and on the first bite your tongue burns and then fizzles. No. This place has what you need. My mouth was sizzling and my husband turned red and was sweating from the heat of these drunken noodles. He was grateful the chef rightfully guessed he would like his meal "mild flame". The only reason I didn't finish my plate was because it was soooooo hot. But I LOVED it. We will definitely be back there! Likely tomorrow for more 🥰 Thai Cafe - can't wait to see you again soon!!!

I have been dining at Zab since they opened, having been thrilled that a Thai restaurant opened close by (I have since moved from Loveland to Morrow, but I still order from Zab). I have been to Thai restaurants all over the States and also many, many different countries.

The food is nearly always fresh, consistently well spiced, and delicious. Years ago my first introduction to Thai food was "Bangkok Thai" in Milford, which has since changed names a myriad of times and is probably closed. I was hooked on the first bite and this was at least 15 years ago - yes friends, Thai food is THAT good!

Zab's does nearly all of their dishes well. I have tried many of the dishes on the menu, and unsurprisingly I go for the Pad Thai most of the time (4 out of 5 hot with beef, not chicken, which is unusual but I enjoy it!). I always get a side order of Spring Rolls and I have to say they make the BEST Spring Rolls I have ever had from a Thai restaurant. So fresh, perfectly cooked, great balance, and a tremendously delicious dipping sauce.

I have also had the Basil Noodles which are wonderful (but not a "regular" order for me at least), the Holy Basil, the Braised Pork, and finally - and possibly one of their best dishes - the Massaman Curry. I have never been disappointed with the food whatsoever, but of course some dishes are better than others. There is a reason they list things like the Massaman Curry under "Specialties" - because they know how to make it very damn well!

All in all, an unassuming but delicious restaurant that has been around long enough now to have made a name for itself. Yes, it's in a strip mall. Yes, most people would assume it would be "meh" and just barely acceptable. But that ain't the truth folks - this place is a gem, a diamond in the rough. Strip mall and preconceived notions be damned; this is a genuine five star Thai restaurant.

I hope you enjoy it as much as I have over the years. I wrote this review because I just placed an order for takeout and you know what? I have no concerns whatsoever - indeed, I know it's going to be delicious, and I simply can't wait to chow down!

I do wish their kao soy (also sometimes spelled khao soi) was more similar to the type found commonly in northern Thailand. Traditionally, it's a chicken leg stewed until tender in a lighter curry soup-like broth. It features both boiled and crispy fried noodles with diced red onion or shallots, lime slices, and fermented greens or cabbage on the side.

This broth is noticeably creamier and more coconut-flavored with different spices than the one that has become my favorite Thai dish. After seeing a movie at the theater across the parking lot, Big Bowl sounded like a great way to end the evening. We were early, around 5:30 PM, and there was a wait. But, there were a few seats open at the bar so we took them right away.

I have been here before, but it has been many years - before I began to use Yelp. So, first check-in and first review.

The bartender was not new at Big Bowl, but it was his first evening shift and he did a great job. He was very attentive and personable which made the evening pleasant. We ordered a couple of drinks and we each decided to get their stir-fry.

If you have not been to Big Bowl or a restaurant like it, you get into a line, grab a bowl, and select your vegetables. Here, unlike other places I've been to, you choose your protein and sauce before going up - you take your ticket and, after filling your bowl, you place the bowl on top of your ticket for the chefs.

Why three stars? The food was really outstanding. And, as said above, so was the server. When our food arrived and I tasted it, I realized that they must have given me someone else's. So, someone got my very spicy curry with Chow Fun noodles, and I got a very sweet dish with udon noodles. The pineapple really gave it away. The server took care of it right away - made sure he took my order again, made sure we were not double-charged, and I had the food remade. When it came out this time, it was right. A few minutes later, they even brought me another one... (They tried to serve me someone else's again.) We really had a good laugh over that one.

Altogether, it was a good experience and we will return. I would say, based on taste, the food was four stars. The service was mixed - the server/bartender gets 5 stars from me. But, Big Bowl needs to get their act together about who they serve what. Yes, they took care of it, but I'm certain that the first meal they served wound up in the trash. I don't know about the third one. Wasted food is disappointing.

Now please note, I have been to another Big Bowl location in the city years ago and I have been to similar concepts before but that didn’t prevent me from being thoroughly confused much to the entertainment of my wife.

Our server was either off or a bit aloof but was not awesome as we waited a bit to be served after a brief greeting and then took a drink order which I later had to remind him to grab my beer from the bar. Also, places like this I like a “Have you been here before?” since it is somewhat of a concept place and even if I say “YES” you explain it to me again.

First, we got her Pot Stickers as an appetizer, which in hindsight I am sure she would love to have not had to share and would have eaten a few plates. Sauce was good and had they had a little crisp to them.

Now the entertainment. I fully intended to make my own Big Bowl so I thought like other places, I just head up and start making it like a buffet. Much to my surprise when my wife was telling the server what protein she wanted and sauce and rice/noodles. She looked at me all surprised I wasn’t ready but I didn’t read the directions and I was used to being a sauce mixologist when making my bowl. Not a deal breaker but I was confused to say the least. We got in line and I missed the whole “you get your own tongs” and noticed after I was already holding up the line while further entertaining my wife and other patron in line who was amused that someone let me out in public. I got my bowl nice and full but I do miss the explanation on the glass of what each item was, I do know my veggies but when you have 3 different mushroom, I’d like to know what is what. Also, not really a big bowl, Big Bowl! But really, it was plenty of food.

Hi, Randy.  I appreciate your concern, and also understand why a less than perfect rating is discouraging.  It is clear when we dine at Pangea, your entire staff takes great pride in creating a unique dining experience.  With that being said, these are a few reasons we (it was my family as a whole who rated) decided on 4 stars:
1.  At the cash register, you had displayed cans of Joia, which we were interested in trying.  My daughter and I discussed (in front of the cashier) which flavor we would split.  When I ordered it, the cashier told me you don't currently have those in stock.  On her behalf, she suggested instead High Noon, which we did try and enjoyed.  But, why display items that you don't have?
2.  My daughters and I are big macaron fans, and sometimes come in just for dessert!  We love the fact that you have such a variety.  Recently, my daughter noticed there were 2 colors of her favorite flavor, chocolate.  I do know how temperamental they are to make.  Over mixing, ingredient ratios not perfect, or inconsistent oven temperatures can all result in dull cookies.  In this case, the few remaining duller ones were on top of the shiny, vibrant cookies.  We were served a dull one.  It gave the impression you were trying to get rid of the ugly ducklings.  Although she said it was still delicious, my daughter expressed disappointment of the visual difference.  I think it would have been best to hold the shiny ones until the others had sold out so that we didn't have the comparison.
3.  Finally, the last issue has been ongoing.  My husband and I have come to your restaurant many times to split a Pistachio Pizza.  That flavor combination was just incredible to us!  A month or better ago, we came in for lunch.  For both of us, we couldn't put our finger on it, but something with the pizza was different.  It was still good, but it just didn't have the same "wow factor" as before.  Shortly thereafter, a coworker came to Pangea for the first time (after hearing both my husband and I brag about that pizza).  She, unfortunately, was not pleased with it.  On my most recent visit, I once again ordered the Pistachio, hoping our previous issue was a fluke.  Again, the flavor profile was not the same, and this time, my hands were left sticky from (I assume) an excess amount of the honey drizzle.  I can't say what has changed - only you would know that.  But, next time, we will order something different.
Please understand, these are only mild criticisms, as far as we're concerned. We are still fans of your restaurant, and certainly hope you have longevity because of the delicious creativity your restaurant has brought to the east side!  I hope my feedback helps.

In the former Excalibur space which was owned by Dennis Rodman, the Tao Group did not disappoint with keeping the extravagant tradition of the theme of Tao restaurants. It has to be seen to be believed. It is truly a sight. My husband & I decided to go for our wedding anniversary. We were nicely greeted at the door by the doorman who instructed us where to go once inside the huge castle like doors. Up the stairs we were then greeted by coat check to which I happily obliged. The hostess offered us two table options, one of which was available right away & the other a slight wait. We decided to wait for the more private booth & scurried to the bar for a cocktail. The drinks & bar service were fantastic. The bar & skyboxes resting above the dining room are nicely separated from the main area. The nightclub is atop of both. The gigantic Quan Yin statue (or Guanyin if you want to be more specific) is your centerpiece. The beautiful 3D projections laid over the structure never seemed to repeat.
The food was quite impressive. We went on a bustling Tuesday. The place was packed & our reservation was at 8:30. We got tons of food including the delicious lobster wontons, crispy rice tuna, shrimp tempura roll with honey wasabi & more. We also had the yellowfin tuna tacos which I was not impressed with due to their extreme blandness. Everything else was superb. Our server, Britney was nice & showed enthusiasm in the beginning of our service but seemed to lose it as the night went on. I don't know if something happened or if we just weren't ordering the way she would've preferred but everyone else was very nice & helpful. We still left a proper, solid tip despite the slight disappointment & will definitely be back to try all the other menu items we couldn't fit into our stomach on this particular night. The cocktails featuring red bull should probably stick to night club drinks only. They could stand to turn the music down just a couple of notches for the dinner crowd. Next time I think we'll plant at the bar & do our ordering there.

I used my chopsticks and a lot of patience to loosen the noodles to the best of my ability. There were still some chucks of noodles as you can see in the pictures. Also I ordered a Thai tea bubble tea and it came in a dome lid even though the drink wasn't a frozen drink. I was shocked to see the nickel size hole on the lid was not sealed/covered in any way when now every restaurants are putting in effort to ensure their foods are probably sealed. They also did not give me a bubble tea straw (bigger than normal straw for the tapioca pearls). The sauces for the apps were in tiny sauce containers which made dipping difficult.

Response to the restaurant's comment:
I guess it's okay for you to stand by your choice of how you pack the noodles and defend yourself just like I have a choice to not give you my business.
